newsitem.title: FRANCE: Algeria's population rises to 29 million in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Algeria's population rises to 29 million in 1996.

text.p: Algeria's population rose to 28.9 million at the end of 1996, up by 600,000 on 1995, the Algerian official news agency APS said on Tuesday.

APS, quoting the government-run National Statistics Office (ONS), said there were 80,000 fewer babies born in 1996, following a trend of a slowing birth rate. Births in 1995 totalled 711,000, down by 65,000 on the 776,000 births in 1994.

Despite the fall in the birth rate, more Algerians got married in 1995, APS said, but gave no figure for 1996. The number of new married couples increased by 5,235 to 153,792 in 1995 from 148,557 in 1994.
APS gave no more specific figures for population in 1996.
Earlier official figures showed Algeria's population growth rate swung slightly under 2.0 percent in 1996 from an average 3.4 percent for the past three decades.

The Algerian government still sees the roughly 2.0 percent increase each year as a factor in compounding the country's social crisis with more than 28 percent unemployement and a shortage of more than one million housing units.
Algerian officials blame poverty and other social woes for driving many young Algerians into the ranks of Moslem guerrillas locked with security forces in a five-year-old civil strife.
